All your nbn® plan questions answered

What nbn® speed do I need?

For one or two people browsing and streaming, nbn® 25 is enough. For a family streaming across several devices, choose nbn® 50. If you work from home, game, or have ten or more devices connected, nbn® 500 or nbn® 1000 will handle it comfortably.

How do I get connected with Swoop?

Just two simple steps to connect.

Step 1: Check my address. Enter your address here to see if you can connect to the nbn®, then choose a plan based on your technology type.

Step 2: Get connected. If your nbn® is already active, our friendly support team simply provisions your connection. Timing depends on your technology type, and for FTTP households it can be done within a few hours. Plug your new Swoop router into the data point (or set up your existing router) and enjoy life in the fast lane.

Installation (if required). Some addresses need an nbn® technician to finalise the connection first. If so, you just book a time slot that suits you, and once the work is done you are ready to go.

Can I get nbn® fibre to the premises?

If your address is on FTTN or FTTC you may be eligible for a $0 fibre upgrade to FTTP. You trigger the upgrade by ordering an eligible high-speed plan, and we coordinate the rest with NBN Co. New developments may attract a $300 NBN Co new development charge.

Check your address here to see if you qualify for a $0 fibre upgrade.

What is a good upload speed for nbn®?

A good upload speed depends on what you send, not just what you download. A video call needs around 3 Mbps, and cloud backups or large file uploads need more. Our nbn® 25 plan provides a typical evening upload speed of 9 Mbps, nbn® 50 provides 18 Mbps, nbn® 500 provides 42 Mbps and nbn® 1000 provides 96 Mbps. If you work from home, choose nbn® 500 or faster. See our nbn® speeds explained guide.

How much do Swoop’s nbn® plans cost?

Our plans start at $54 per month for nbn® 25 for your first six months, then $69 ongoing. nbn® 50 is $69, nbn® 500 is $72 and nbn® 1000 is $85, each for your first six months. Every plan includes unlimited data and no lock-in contract.

What is an unlimited nbn® plan?

An unlimited plan has no data cap, so you are never charged excess data fees. Every nbn® plan we offer includes unlimited data. We do not meter your usage or slow your speed once you reach a threshold.

Can I change or cancel my nbn® plan?

Yes. Every plan is month to month with no lock-in contract and no cancellation fee*. You can upgrade at any time, and downgrade from the first day of your next billing cycle. There is no charge to change plans at the same address.

Do I need a modem for my nbn® plan?

Yes, you need a modem or router to connect. You can bring your own, or add one to your plan. We offer the TP-Link VR400 v3, and eero 7 for gigabit speeds across your whole home. eero 7 is available on all our FTTP fibre plans.

What are the nbn® technology types?

Your address connects using one of five technologies: fibre to the premises (FTTP), fibre to the node (FTTN), fibre to the building (FTTB), fibre to the curb (FTTC) or hybrid fibre coaxial (HFC).

On FTTN, FTTB and FTTC your speed is capped at 100 Mbps. You may be eligible for a $0 fibre upgrade.

Enter your address here and we will show you which of our internet plans you can order.

What happens to my nbn® service if I move house?

Let us know before you move and we will transfer your nbn® service to your new address. Your plan and speed depend on the technology available there, so check your new address first.

See our moving home guide for the full process.

Is nbn® available in all Australian capital cities?

Yes. The nbn® network reaches all eight Australian capital cities — Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, Hobart, Darwin and Canberra — with the national rollout completed in 2020. Capital cities have essentially universal coverage, though the technology type at your address can vary.

Check your address here to see the plans and speeds you’re eligible for.
